newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Embattled Karabakh enclave goes to polls.
newsitem.headline: Embattled Karabakh enclave goes to polls.

text.p: The mostly ethnic Armenian population of Azerbaijan's embattled enclave of Nagorno-Karabakh went to the polls on Sunday in a presidential election which the current regional leader is expected to win.
An uneasy ceasefire in the mountainous Caucasus region has prevailed since May 1994, six years after its unilateral declaration of independence from Azerbaijan.
Local journalists in the regional capital Stepanakert, contacted by telephone from the Armenian capital Yerevan, said voting appeared to be going smoothly, with a healthy turnout.
By 1300 GMT, four hours before the 171 polling stations close, half the electorate of 89,000 had cast their ballots.

Western countries have joined Azeri President Haydar Aliyev in condemning the vote, saying it could jepoardise peace talks involving Armenia and Azerbaijan. Karabakh makes no secret of its desire to join Armenia. Azerbaijan refuses to consider anything more than autonomy for the region.

Robert Kocharyan, who two years ago was elected president of the self-declared republic, is widely expected to win a new, five-year mandate. Standing against him are Boris Arushayan and communist leader Grant Melkumyan.
The Azeri authorities in Baku have criticised the election, as have a number of Western countries, including France, which on Friday said the polls would complicate peace talks.
Fighting, in which Christian ethnic Armenians drove mainly Moslem Azeris out and set the former Soviet states of Armenia and Azerbaijan at loggerheads, claimed over 10,000 lives.
On Friday, Armenia and Azerbaijan failed again to agree on resolving the conflict after talks in Helsinki.
